cards.explanation: The job is to prophesy with instruments, friends. David and the commanders set these sons apart "…to prophesy with the accompaniment of lyres, harps, and cymbals." (1 Chronicles 25:1) So the assignment is prophesying, and the instruments go right along with it. I love that.

The answer is True. The text says Asaph "…prophesied under the direction of the king." (1 Chronicles 25:2) So the sons answer to their father, and their father answers to the king. Everybody in this band has somebody to answer to, friends.

Jeduthun is giving thanks and praise to the LORD, friends. The text says he "…prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD." (1 Chronicles 25:3) Thanks and praise, with a harp in his hands. I think that's a fine way to spend a day.

The answer is to exalt him, bakers. The text says these sons were given to Heman "…through the promises of God to exalt him…" (1 Chronicles 25:5) It's a promise, and the children came with it. I think that's a whole lot of reasons to smile.

All that music is for the service of the house of God, friends. The text says they were under their fathers' direction "for the music of the house of the LORD…for the service of the house of God." (1 Chronicles 25:6) All those cymbals and harps were for that house. No small gig.

The word is songs, bakers. The relatives were "…all trained and skillful in the songs of the LORD…" (1 Chronicles 25:7) Trained AND skillful. These folks practiced, and I'm proud of every one of them.

The answer is False, friends. The text says they cast lots for their duties, "…young and old alike, teacher as well as pupil." (1 Chronicles 25:8) The teachers drew a lot just like the students. I think that's a good way to keep everybody on equal footing.
